title: Molar photon energy
hints: A mole contains Avogadro’s number of photons.
Divide joules by 1000 to get kilojoules.
Compare the result with each choice and check its sign, units, or underlying rule.
statement:
A photon has $4.00\times10^{-19}$ J. Using $N_A=6.022\times10^{23}$, what is the energy of one mole of these photons?

[_]{a}

explanations: Multiply by Avogadro’s constant and convert J to kJ.
The powers of ten are off by three.
This numeric value is in J/mol.
